'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**[[Houthi movement|Houthi]] forces storm the former [[United States]] [[embassy]] in [[Sanaa]], [[Yemen]], taking several Yemeni staffers [[hostage]] and removing "large quantities of equipment and materials" from the [[diplomat]]ic facility. [https://news.yahoo.com/houthi-rebels-storm-u-embassy-173519204.html (''National Review'' via Yahoo! News)]
*[[Internal conflict in Myanmar]]
**The Catholic cathedral Sacred Heart at [[Pekon]] in the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Pekhon|Diocese of Pekhon]] in Burma’s [[Shan State|Shan state]] was among several structures that were reportedly hit by military artillery fire on Nov. 9 amid continuing armed clashes between government and rebel forces. [https://www.catholicnewsagency.com/news/249561/catholic-cathedral-hit-by-artillery-shelling-in-burma (Catholic News Agency)] [http://www.fides.org/en/news/71112-ASIA_MYANMAR_A_Catholic_church_hit_by_rockets_Baptist_churches_burned_down (Fides)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[Social impact of the COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
**As many as 57,000 [[Nursing home|care home]] workers are [[dismissal (employment)|fired]] or [[resign]] as the [[government of the United Kingdom|government]]'s new "no jab, no job" mandate enters into force in [[England]], which requires care home workers in England, including cleaners and receptionists, to be fully [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccinated]] against [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/society/2021/nov/11/england-care-home-workers-on-mandatory-covid-vaccines (''The Guardian'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[November 2021 India and Sri Lanka floods]]
**Twenty-five people in [[Sri Lanka]] and 16 people in [[India]] are killed by [[flood]]s that have been affecting both countries in recent days. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/heavy-rains-expected-ease-india-sri-lanka-25-dead-2021-11-11/ (Reuters)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****[[Beijing]] imposes new restrictions on conferences and events, recommending that both be held remotely and also recommending that in-person conferences be managed as a "closed loop" after the city reported six new locally transmitted COVID-19 cases in the past 24 hours. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/beijing-city-imposes-covid-restrictions-conferences-events-2021-11-11/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] begins the world's first nationwide COVID-19 drill named "Omega Drill" consisting of three sessions that will test the country's preparation for the possible outbreak of a new and more lethal variant of the virus. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-11-11/israel-holds-war-games-to-prepare-for-more-lethal-covid-strain (Bloomberg News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vietnam]]
****[[Vietnam]] surpasses one million cases of COVID-19. [https://ampe.vnexpress.net/news/news/vietnam-coronavirus-tally-tops-1-million-4384583.html (''VnExpress International'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in France]]
****France reports a new [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|strain of SARS-CoV-2]], known as lineage B.1.X or B.1.640, which was first found on 15 October in a school in [[Bannalec]] in the north-western region of [[Brittany]], where 24 people got infected; but it was only identified to be a separate strain until much later. The origin of the Bannalec outbreak seemed to be a man in [[Nantes]] who had come from abroad a few days before. No cases related to the strain were reported since October 26, but it remains under surveillance. ([https://www.jpost.com/health-and-wellness/coronavirus/new-covid-variant-found-in-france-reason-for-panic-or-not-quite-yet-684878 ''Jerusalem Post''])
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****Germany reports a record for the second consecutive day of 50,196 new cases of COVID-19. [https://www.cnbc.com/2021/11/11/germany-covid-cases-hit-50000-a-day-prompting-100000-deaths-warning.html (CNBC)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Netherlands]]
****Following several record-breaking daily increases in new COVID-19 cases, including a record 16,364 new cases reported in the past 24 hours, the [[government of the Netherlands|government]] deliberates on potential partial [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] scenarios, which if enacted would be the first partial lockdowns in [[Western Europe]] since the summer. [https://www.barrons.com/news/dutch-report-record-daily-new-covid-cases-01636641907?refsec=afp-news (AFP via ''Barron's'')]
***[[European Union response to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****The [[European Medicines Agency]] approves the two antibody cocktails named [[Ronapreve]] made by [[Roche]] and [[Regeneron]], and [[Regkirona]] made by [[Celltrion]] to treat severe COVID-19 patients. [https://medicalxpress.com/news/2021-11-eu-watchdog-covid-antibody-treatments.html (Medical Xpress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Oceania]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]], [[COVID-19 vaccination in Australia]]
****The number of people over the age of 16 years old in Australia who have received their first dose of the COVID-19 [[vaccine]] surpasses 90%. [https://7news.com.au/lifestyle/vaccines/australia-reaches-90-per-cent-first-dose-vaccine-benchmark-c-4515054 (''Seven News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Fiji]]
****[[Fiji]] reopens its borders to travel partners, fully vaccinated [[tourism in Fiji|tourists]] and diplomats, and people who pass a [[risk assessment]]. [https://www.rnz.co.nz/international/pacific-news/455438/fiji-reopens-international-borders (RNZ Pacific)]

'''International relations'''
*[[Belarus–Ukraine relations]], [[2021 Belarus–European Union border crisis]]
**[[Ukraine]] deploys a further 8,500 [[Ukrainian Ground Forces|soldiers]] and police officers, as well as 15 helicopters, to the [[Belarus–Ukraine border|border]] with [[Belarus]] to prevent possible attempts by stranded migrants to cross into the country in order to reach the [[European Union]]. [https://www.voanews.com/a/ukraine-to-deploy-troops-helicopters-to-guard-belarus-border-/6309168.html (Voice of America)]
**[[President of Belarus|Belarusian President]] [[Alexander Lukashenko]] says he "would recommend the leadership of [[Poland]], [[Lithuania|Lithuanians]] and other empty-headed people to think before speaking," suggesting Belarus would halt [[natural gas]] supplies into Europe, if the EU pushes more sanctions. EU member states are to decide some time next week on new sanctions for [[human trafficking]] which led to the crisis. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-59256927 (BBC News)]
*[[Mali–Russia relations]]
**[[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Mali)|Malian Foreign Affairs minister]] [[Abdoulaye Diop]] says that [[Mali]] "may ask [[Russia]] for help" due to [[Mali War|the country's security situation]], with Diop also saying that "the very existence of the [[Politics of Mali|Malian state]] is under threat". [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/mali-says-it-may-ask-russia-help-given-current-security-situation-2021-11-11/ (Reuters)]
*[[Foreign relations of Tuvalu]]
**[[Tuvalu]]an [[Cabinet of Tuvalu|Justice, Communication and Foreign Affairs Minister]] [[Simon Kofe]] announces that the [[island nation]] will push to retain [[Diplomatic recognition|international recognition]] of its statehood and [[maritime border]]s in the event that [[Sea level rise|rising sea levels]] completely submerge the country. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2021/nov/11/tuvalu-seeks-to-retain-statehood-if-it-sinks-completely-as-sea-levels-rise (''The Guardian'')]
